% Pattern: head/case. A \paragraph in a proof whose title reads as a proof
% that proves nothing, as "Proof for $N=2$", or as an item numbered by a
% reference, as "Property \ref{small}", is a case of the proof named by its
% title. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want lemma-1 statement/lemma 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=lemma-1
% want head-1 other/case -
% want head-2 other/case -
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}
\begin{document}
We work with finite sets.
\begin{lemma}\label{small}
Every finite set is small.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma \ref{small}]
We divide the proof by the size of the set.

\paragraph{Proof for $N=2$.} The two points bound the set.

\paragraph{Property \ref{small}:}
The bound holds for each point.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
